item.title: MEPs block move to cut passenger compensation for flight delays in Europe
item.description: The European parliament on Wednesday rejected plans to allow airlines to incur longer flight delays before having to compensate passengers, locking horns with member states that have backed the move.

item.title: 19-year-old jailed for plot to attack Stockholm festival
item.description: A Stockholm court on Wednesday jailed a 19-year-old for nearly eight years for having plotted to attack a culture festival on behalf of the Islamic State.

item.title: Sweden denying study permits for high-school exchange programs
item.description: Leading student exchange organizations have had major problems with the Swedish Migration Agency over the past two years, The Local reports, with 16-year-olds from non-EU countries regularly denied permits to spend an exchange year studying in Sweden.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Thursday
item.description: Swedish stock market expected to rise after Trump drops tariff threat, more Christmas presents bought online, and other news from Sweden on Thursday.

item.title: Sweden says it will not participate in Trump's 'Board of Peace'
item.description: Sweden's prime minister Ulf Kristersson has confirmed that Sweden will not join US President Donald Trump's so-called Board of Peace, "as the text currently stands".

item.title: Swedish pension fund sells off US Treasury bonds
item.description: Swedish pension fund Alecta said Wednesday that it had sold the bulk of its US Treasury bonds over the past year, citing the unpredictability of the current administration and growing US debt.

item.title: How Trump-proof is Sweden's economy?
item.description: Sweden's finance minister Elisabeth Svantesson declared the Swedish economy was "Trump-proof" when US President Trump said on Monday that he would hit Sweden with tariffs. The tariff threat was dropped on Wednesday, but how vulnerable is the Sweden to future tariffs?

item.title: Sweden's plan to revoke existing permanent residency permits on hold
item.description: Plans to revoke permanent residency permits for more than 100,000 foreign citizens in Sweden appear to be on hold, after a government spokesperson said the proposal would not be included in this spring’s bills as it is “still being analysed.”

item.title: 'They show me pity': Americans in Sweden describe treatment in wake of Trump threats
item.description: Most Swedes don't treat them differently on a personal level, say our American readers, although many describe having to answer more questions about their government than before. And some resent Swedish assumptions that they don't support Trump.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: pudla
item.description: The verb pudla comes from pudel, the Swedish word for a poodle. Despite this, it doesn’t have much to do with fluffy dogs.
